$comment: The completeness contract. 7 fixed item types; each type declares the facets (checklist) its text must cover. plan.py uses this to print gap reports and drive the agent's detail-filling pass; lock.py uses parts of it for structural validation (refs resolve, fields present, min length). Facet coverage itself is semantic — checked by the plan-pass LLM lint + human diff review, never by fragile keyword matching (decisions.md §4.4).

character.role: character identity lock. Repeat verbatim in every shot that shows the character. Never two character items for the same body.

state.role: world or character state VARIABLE — a dated variant that exists at a specific timeline point. A fact change must be a new state item, never an override (decisions.md §3.5).

scene.role: scene base — the fixed description of a location. Repeated verbatim by every shot in that location so the world does not drift.

set_piece.role: fixed prop / stage device that lives in a scene. One item per object. Do not fold a prop into a scene item (drift risk).

look.role: lighting + atmosphere together — one item manages both so light and mood never get described twice by different items.

style.role: project style lock — art direction, aspect ratio, grade. Repeated in every prompt.

camera_grammar.role: optional editing/camera conventions as text (e.g. hard cuts land on bar lines, handheld only for close-ups).

rules: shots with non-empty lyric_lines MUST have a non-empty lyric_intent (decisions.md §5.1)
shots MUST reference at least one character item and one scene item
overrides may only append emphasis to an item — never replace it (decisions.md §3.5)
every automated cut lands on a bar line (beatmap grid)
